messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated latency detected for streaming and generation endpoints in eu-west region. p99 > 2s, error rate climbing. Paging SRE oncall.

alex.r: I’m on call and saw the page. starting triage — can folks drop initial p95/p99 numbers and impacted routes?

jon.p: quick snapshot from dashboards: baseline p95 ~ 220ms / p99 ~ 420ms. Right now p95 ~ 480ms / p99 ~ 2.3s for /v1/stream and /v1/generate. Streaming stalls metric spiked from 0.3% -> ~12% in last 7m. links: <https://grafana/redwood/d/streams?panelId=4>

net-eng: I’m seeing elevated packet retransmits and short bursts of packet loss on cross-AZ paths between azb <-> azc in eu-west-2. Also NAT SNAT table saturation in azc for our egress subnets (high ephemeral port reuse).

sre-oncall: copying checks to run: `ss -tan | grep :443 | wc -l` to measure connections, `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` to check NAT table size, and `mtr -r -c 50 ${peer_ip}` for cross-AZ loss.

alex.r: running those now.

alex.r: paste: ```
ss -tan | grep :443 | wc -l
> 12712
conntrack -L | wc -l
> 65532
```

alex.r: conntrack looks near limits, lots of TIME_WAIT entries. net-eng, can you confirm NAT gateway metrics?

net-eng: Confirmed. NAT gateway in azc showing port exhaustion high -> returning 502/504 on some flows and causing TLS handshakes to stall. Cloud metrics: SNAT ports used > 98% on azc.ngw-03. Packet loss on the azb->azc link about 1.8% in spikes.

mira.t: I’ll take this incident from Alex. Alex — handing on-call. Mira now leading triage.

alex.r: handing to Mira. I’ll stay on slack to help.

mira.t: ok. mitigation plan options: (1) create new NAT gateway in azc and update route table / target groups to split traffic, (2) temporarily shift egress for some subnets to azb NAT that has free ports, (3) tune conntrack timeout aggressively for short-lived flows to free up ports while we stabilize. Which do we want first?

net-eng: fastest: shift egress for affected subnets to azb NAT (already healthy) — update route table. Also provision new NAT in parallel. Conntrack timeout tweak is risky but doable for a short window: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait=30` (current default 120s).

mira.t: execute option 2 now then create new NAT. Priya/CS — can you draft a short status for affected customers? We should say we’re investigating networking-related latency and streaming stalls, engineering mitigation in progress.

priya.s: on it. Drafting: "We’re investigating increased latency and streaming stalls affecting some EU customers. Engineers are actively mitigating; we’ll post updates in 15 minutes." Will post to customers after we confirm mitigation step started.

net-eng: executing route table change to shift egress for subnet svc-eu-west-2a -> azb-ngw

```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0a1b2c --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-azb-ngw-01
```

net-eng: route change applied in azc subnets. Verifying connections.

jon.p: after route change: p95 dropped ~320ms, p99 down to ~1.1s, streaming stalls down to ~3.5%. Partial mitigation observed.

mira.t: good. Keep the new routing in place while we provision a dedicated NAT in azc. Also create CloudWatch alarm for SNAT port usage > 90% for all AZs.

net-eng: provisioning new NAT in azc now. Also rolling an automated conntrack cleanup job on affected hosts to reclaim time_wait entries: `conntrack -F` (careful — this will drop flows). We'll run during maintenance window but can do targeted flush for service IP ranges.

alex.r: is there any evidence this is caused by app-level connection growth (bad client keepalives) vs infra-level NAT limit?

jon.p: connection histograms show a bursty tail — roughly doubling concurrent TLS sessions from a subset of customers after a release earlier today. So likely a mix: traffic increase + NAT port exhaustion made it visible as p99 and stalls.

priya.s: CS update posted to customers: "Mitigation in progress; routing change applied; partial improvement observed. We will update in 15m or sooner."

mira.t: action items: 1) net-eng finish NAT creation in azc, 2) engineering to review client connection behavior and release from today (rollback if needed), 3) CS continue customer comms, 4) open postmortem and RCA.

net-eng: new NAT gateway created and associated with azc route tables. SNAT usage falling to comfortable levels.

jon.p: current metrics: p95 ~ 260ms, p99 ~ 820ms, streaming stalls ~2%. Error rate back down close to baseline.

mira.t: marking incident as mitigated for customer-facing impact. We’ll keep monitoring for 2 hours. Assigning follow-ups: ENG-2467 (client connection regression review), INFRA-1122 (NAT capacity autoscale and alarm tuning), PM-ops to update runbook.

priya.s: customer comms: posted status update and notified top 5 affected customers directly. They acknowledged and appreciate quick mitigation.

alex.r: quick notes for postmortem: cross-AZ packet loss + NAT port exhaustion + traffic increase from release = cascading tail latency and streaming stalls. Need durable fixes: autoscale NAT/egress, better conntrack defaults, and guardrails on client connection patterns.

mira.t: agreed. I’ll start incident doc and fill in timeline. tagging :white_check_mark: — moving to monitoring / RCA phase.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity: HIGH, status: mitigated -> in RCA. Create postmortem ticket: https://redwood/ops/incidents/1812500000

cs-team: thanks team. leaving channel for followups in #postmortems."
